subject: Efik
examFormat: Two papers taken as a composite at one sitting; rubrics are written in Efik and answers are in Efik using the standard orthography and metalanguage. Paper 1 is 60 multiple-choice items (Language 30, Literature 22, Culture 8) in 1 hour for 60 marks. Paper 2 is an essay test in three sections (Language, Literature, Culture): six questions in all (three from Section A, two from Section B, one from Section C) in 2 hours for 100 marks.
excluded: Lists of selected and harmonized Efik texts for 2014-2015 and 2016-2020, selected poems and reference books (set books change; described generically).

topics.name: Composition and Letter Writing (Efik)
objectives: Write a narrative essay
Write a descriptive essay
Write an argumentative essay
Write an expository essay
Write a dialogue
Write a debate
Write a letter
topics.content: Candidates are advised to write about 300 words and spend not more than 45 minutes on this section. The topics chosen will include any of the listed essay types: narrative, descriptive, argumentative, expository, dialogue, debate, letter writing.

topics.name: Sound System (Efik)
objectives: Explain the production of vowels and consonants in terms of place and manner of articulation
Classify vowels and consonants phonetically and phonemically
Describe syllable structure: the way consonants and vowels combine in words
Explain sound processes, e.g. vowel harmony, assimilation, elision, deletion
Describe the distribution of sounds in the environments of occurrence (initially, medially and finally)
Explain the adaptation of loanwords
Describe tone and intonation: high, low, falling and rising tones
topics.content: Candidates answer one question out of the two set. Example given in the syllabus: /ọ/ in ọbọñ (king) and ọkọ (fence).

topics.name: Grammar (Efik)
objectives: Explain word structure and word formation: root, affixes (prefix, suffix), compounding, borrowing, reduplication, etc.
Identify word classes: noun, verbs, adverbs, pronouns, adjectives, etc.
Explain grammatical categories: number, person, tense, negation, etc.
Describe the types and functions of phrases and clauses
Describe the structure and types of sentences
topics.content: Candidates answer one question out of the two set.

topics.name: Oral Literature (Efik)
objectives: Show knowledge of the set books on oral prose (folktales, legends, proverbs, riddles, etc.)
Show knowledge of the set books on oral poetry (songs, ballads)
Show knowledge of the set books on oral drama (traditional drama)
topics.content: Three set books cover the different genres. One question is set on each and candidates answer any one.

topics.name: Written Literature (Efik)
objectives: Show knowledge of the set books on written prose, poetry and drama
topics.content: Three set books cover the different genres. One question is set on each and candidates answer any one of the three.

topics.name: Edu Uwem (Customs)
topics.content: Section C: two questions on customs and institutions, candidates answer one. Customs (Edu uwem): (i) Mme ubọk utom (occupations): ukọ iyak, utọ inwaṅ, unyam urua, utom usọ. (ii) Ukpep nti edu uwem ye mme ufon mmọ (good upbringing and its benefits): udia ye edu utem/unam udia nte (enamde kadi, enamdi fufu, ebokde mme efere, etemde ekpaṅ ṅkukwọ). (iii) uduọk mmịn (libation).

topics.name: Nsionsio Nka (Different Institutions)
topics.content: (i) Ubon/ekpuk (family): usuṅ edade ebọk nditọ. (ii) Edu ukpono/se ekponode (worship): Abasi, Ndem, Ibọk, Mbukpo. (iii) Mme nke (proverbs): mme nke etopdetop. (iv) Ubọṅ. (v) Mme ndedịbe nka ke Efịk (secret societies).
